metadata.title: UNDERWATER COMMUNICATION SYSTEM FOR SCUBA DIVERS
metadata.abstract: Underwater wireless communication (UWC) plays a critical role in applications such as tactical surveillance, marine biology monitoring, pollution detection, and underwater infrastructure maintenance. Traditional radio frequency (RF) communication methods, including Wi-Fi, are ineffective underwater due to rapid absorption of radio waves. In contrast, optical wireless communication (OWC) using light, particularly Li-Fi offers a promising alternative, as light can penetrate water more effectively. This paper presents a laser -based underwater communication system designed for real -time audio transmission. Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM) is employed to encode audio signals into laser pulses, which are transmitted through water and received by a solar panel functioning as a photodetector. A comprehensive literature review highlights the use of different laser wavelengths to optimize transmission efficiency, range, and error rates, and discusses acknowledgment mechanisms to detect signal loss. Experimental results demonstrate successful audio transmission in water over a 1 -meter distance and text transmission in air over 5 meters using a line -of-sight setup, with minimal laten cy. Key challenges encountered include beam divergence, water turbidity, and alignment sensitivity. Despite range limitations typically reported in literature (7 –10 meters underwater), our prototype illustrates the potential for low-cost, energy -efficient laser-based systems in applications such as diver communication, marine research, and underwater sensor networks.

pages.text:
UNDERWATER COMMUNICATION SYSTEM 
FOR SCUBA DIVERS 
 
 1Snehal Borhade ,Student, Department Of E &TC Engineering , AISSMS 
COE , Pune , India   saeeborhade1234@gmail.com 
 2Janvi Mahapadi ,Student, Department Of E &TC Engineering , AISSMS 
COE , Pune , India  janvimahapadi@gmail.com 
3Samrudhi Bandi, Student, Department Of E &TC Engineering , AISSMS 
COE , Pune , India  samrudhibandi140@gmail.com 
4Dr. S.B. Dhonde, Head of Department, Department Of E&TC Engineering, 
AISSMS COE Pune, India   sbdhonde@aissmscoe.com  
 
1. Abstract 
Underwater wireless communication (UWC) plays a 
critical role in applications such as tactical surveillance, 
marine biology monitoring, pollution detection, and 
underwater infrastructure maintenance. Traditional radio 
frequency (RF) communication methods, including Wi-
Fi, are ineffective underwater due to rapid absorption of 
radio waves. In contrast, optical wireless communication 
(OWC) using light, particularly Li-Fi offers a promising 
alternative, as light can penetrate water more effectively. 
This paper presents a laser -based underwater 
communication system designed for real -time audio 
transmission. Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM) is 
employed to encode audio signals into laser pulses, which 
are transmitted through water and received by a solar 
panel functioning as a photodetector. A comprehensive 
literature review highlights the use of different laser 
wavelengths to optimize transmission efficiency, range, 
and error rates, and discusses acknowledgment 
mechanisms to detect signal loss. Experimental results 
demonstrate successful audio transmission in water over 
a 1 -meter distance and text transmission in air over 5 
meters using a line -of-sight setup, with minimal laten cy. 
Key challenges encountered include beam divergence, 
water turbidity, and alignment sensitivity. Despite range 
limitations typically reported in literature (7 –10 meters 
underwater), our prototype illustrates the potential for 
low-cost, energy -efficient laser-based systems in 
applications such as diver communication, marine 
research, and underwater sensor networks. 
 
 
 
 
 
2. Introductionn 
Light Fidelity (Li -Fi) is a form of Visible Light 
Communication (VLC) technology developed by 
researchers at the University of Edinburgh. It is an 
emerging wireless communication method that enables 
high-speed data transmission using light-emitting diodes  
(LEDs). Li -Fi operates by modulating the intensity of 
LED light at extremely high speeds—imperceptible to the 
human eye—to encode binary data (1s and 0s). Devices 
equipped with photodiodes can receive this modulated 
light and decode the transmitted informa tion within the 
illumination area. Li -Fi offers several advantages over 
traditional Wi -Fi, including significantly lower latency, 
enhanced data throughput, improved security, and better 
accessibility in environments where radio frequency (RF) 
communication is limited. Under optimal conditions, Li -
Fi has demonstrated data transmission speeds exceeding 
1 Gbps. Additionally, since visible light cannot penetrate 
solid objects such as walls, Li -Fi naturally confines data 
transmission within a physical space, the reby offering 
enhanced data security. Furthermore, the data density of 
Li-Fi is up to 1000 times greater than that of Wi -Fi, 
making it a compelling solution for high -capacity 
wireless communication in densely populated or 
interference-prone environments. 
Effective underwater communication is crucial for 
various applications, including marine research, search 
and rescue operations, environmental monitoring, and 
defence. Traditional communication methods such as 
acoustic and radio frequency (RF) transmission have 
limitations in underwater environments. Acoustic 
communication, while widely used, suffers from low data 
rates, latency, and environmental interference, whereas  
RF signals face high attenuation in water, restricting their 
range and efficiency. Wired communication, though

reliable, limits mobility and flexibility. To overcome 
these challenges, optical communication using lasers has 
emerged as a promising alternative due to its ability to 
achieve high -speed data transfer, minimal latency, and 
efficient energy consumption. 
This project presents a laser -based underwater 
communication system designed to transmit real -time 
audio signals over short to medium distances. The system 
employs a laser transmitter to modulate audio signals 
using Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM). These 
modulated signals are transmitted through water and 
received by a solar panel, which acts as a photo-detector, 
converting the light pulses back into electrical signals. 
The received signals are then processed and amplified to 
produce audio output. Compared  to other optical 
receivers, the use of a solar panel offers a cost -effective 
and power -efficient solution for underwater signal 
detection. 
The effectiveness of laser-based communication depends 
on water clarity, as suspended particles and turbidity can 
cause scattering and absorption, affecting signal quality. 
Despite these challenges, laser communication offers 
several advantages over tradit ional methods, including 
high data transmission rates, narrow beam focus, and 
reduced interference, making it particularly suitable for 
applications in clear water environments. 
This project aims to develop a reliable and efficient 
optical communication system tailored for scuba divers. 
Traditional diver communication methods, such as hand 
signals, are limited by visibility, while acoustic systems 
are often expensive and complex. By leveraging laser 
technology and optical sensors, this system enables light-
based communication, enhancing underwater interactions 
and broadening the scope of underwater data 
transmission. The proposed system has significant 
potential applications, inclu ding diver -to-diver 
communication, underwater sensor networks, marine 
exploration, and defence operations, offering a practical 
and innovative solution for real -time underwater 
connectivity. 
 
3. Literature Review 
 
Various studies have explored underwater 
communication using optical and Li -Fi technologies. A 
paper presented a Li -Fi-based underwater 
communication system that faced challenges with signal 
attenuation and limited range, suggesting improvements 
in transmitter design,[1].  As demonstrated a prototype 
using a red laser and Arduino UNO for text transmission 
over 2 meters, achieving higher data rates than acoustic 
methods but suffering from line -of-sight limitations and 
noise, [9]. A visible light communication system for real-
time audio transmission with a short range of 15 cm, 
suggesting the use of additional LED colors like blue or 
green for extended distance, [4].  A paper even explored 
a 5 Mbps optical wireless communication system with 
error correction coding, proposing a synchronization 
algorithm to ensure reliable data transmission,[3]. An 
underwater communication system for deep -sea divers 
using visible light, highlighting challenges with beam 
spread and recommending optimized transmitter designs. 
These studies collectively underscore the potential of 
optical communication for underwater applications, 
while identifying key areas for enhancement to achieve 
higher data rates, reliability, and extended 
communication range, [5]. The short transmission range 
and signal degradation in deep water, recommending 
advancements to enhance signal strength and mitigate 
environmental interference,[2]. 
 
 
4. Block Diagram 
 
 
Fig. 1: Transmitter Block Diagram 
 
 
 
 
Fig. 2: Receiver Block Diagram 
 
 
5. Methodology 
The proposed underwater communication system for 
scuba divers follows a structured methodology 
encompassing system design, signal transmission and 
reception, and real-time implementation. This approach 
is developed to ensure efficient and reliable audio 
communication using laser-based technology in 
underwater environments.

The system consists of two main components: a 
transmitter and a receiver, both controlled by ESP32 
microcontrollers for signal processing and overall 
coordination. On the transmitter side, audio signals are 
captured using an MAX4466 electret condenser 
microphone. These analog audio signals are then pre-
processed and amplified using a PAM8403 module, 
which also facilitates pulse amplitude modulation 
(PAM). A red laser diode, is used to transmit the 
modulated audio signals through water using optical 
pulses. 
For reception, the system departs from traditional 
methods by employing a solar panel instead of a Light 
Dependent Resistor (LDR) for detecting the laser light. 
The solar panel offers improved sensitivity and faster 
response times under varying underwater lighting 
conditions. When the modulated laser light reaches the 
receiver, the solar panel converts it directly into an 
electrical signal. This signal is then processed by the 
ESP32 microcontroller on the receiver side, which 
performs demodulation and converts the electrical 
signals back into an audio format. A PAM audio 
amplifier is subsequently used to enhance the 
demodulated audio signal, which is then output through 
a speaker for clear sound reproduction. 
To ensure robust communication, an acknowledgment 
mechanism is implemented in the system. This 
mechanism allows the receiver to confirm successful 
reception of the signal. In case of a signal drop or error, 
a feedback signal is sent to the transmitter, prompting it 
to resend the lost data, thereby enhancing 
communication reliability. 
The entire system is implemented and tested using the 
Arduino IDE, which allows real-time simulation and 
debugging. The accuracy and fidelity of the received 
audio signals are evaluated by comparing them with the 
original input. This comparison validates the 
effectiveness of the proposed underwater communication 
system using laser-based transmission and solar panel-
based detection, highlighting its potential for practical 
deployment in underwater scenarios such as scuba 
diving communication. 
Hardware Setup 
The hardware implementation consists of cost -
effective components optimized for real -time 
underwater communication: 
 
1. ESP32-WROOM 32  – Serves as the primary 
processing unit for both the transmitter and 
receiver, handling audio signal processing, 
modulation, and demodulation. 
 
2. MAX4466 Electret Condenser Microphone – 
Captures audio input for transmission through the 
laser communication system. 
3. PAM8403 Module – Amplifies and modulates the 
audio signal using pulse amplitude modulation 
(PAM) for efficient laser transmission. 
4. Laser Diode – Emits a red laser beam carrying the 
modulated audio data, enabling light -based 
communication through water. 
5. Solar Panel  – Acts as the receiver sensor, 
detecting the transmitted laser signals and 
converting them into electrical signals with 
higher sensitivity and faster response than 
traditional LDRs. 
6. Speaker – Outputs the reconstructed audio, 
enabling real -time communication for scuba 
divers. 
7. Power Supply and Supporting Modules  – 
Provide stable and reliable power to all 
components, ensuring continuous operation. 
   Software Setup 
The system is designed to run on the Arduino IDE for 
programming and uploading code to the ESP32 
modules. The software environment ensures efficient 
real-time audio transmission and reception using light-
based communication. 
    Programming Environment 
The Arduino IDE, along with the ESP32 board 
manager and required libraries, is used for coding and 
debugging. The implementation is carried out using 
C/C++ for low -level hardware interaction and real -
time processing. Additional libraries such as SD.h for 
SD card access, SPI.h for communication, and 
driver/gpio.h for laser control are utilized. 
 
 
Fig. 3: Transmitter Circuit

Fig. 4: Receiver Circuit 
 
 
 
 
Technical Details 
 
We used a red laser diode (650nm) with a 6mm size and 
5V operating voltage, achieving a range of over 7 -10 
meters in the air. While blue (450nm) and green (520nm) 
lasers offer greater range in both air and water, they are 
costly and hazardous to humans. Fo r demonstration 
purposes, the red laser was preferred, operating within 3V-
5V. The ESP32 -WROOM module, with an operating 
voltage of 2-3.6V, was selected for its versatile GPIO pins 
supporting functions like digital I/O, PWM, SPI, I²C, 
UART, and interrupts, along with capacitive touch sensing. 
It also features two 12-bit SAR ADCs with 18 channels and 
two 8-bit DACs for analog signal generation. 
 
An Solar Pannel (3.3V-5V) was used for signal detection, 
with its sensitivity adjusted based on environmental 
conditions. The demonstration was conducted in a dark 
room to minimize interference, and a 1 -meter-long tube 
was used as a controlled environment filled with either air 
or water. Arduino IDE was used to program the ESP32, 
implementing a basic algorithm to convert text into bits. 
The red laser transmits these bits via light signals, which 
are then detected and decoded using another ESP32 
module paired with the LDR sensor. 
 
The audio transmission system was implemented using a 
MAX4466 electret microphone module to capture analog 
audio signals. These signals were then amplified and 
modulated using a PAM8403 audio amplifier module. A 
7805 voltage regulator was incorporated into the circuit to 
provide a stable 5V power supply to the components. The 
modulated audio signal was used to drive a laser diode, 
which served as the optical transmitter. The laser output 
was connected to the output ter minal of the PAM8403 
module, enabling real-time audio transmission via visible 
light. 
 
 
For implementing acknowledgment functionality, both the 
laser transmitter and the microphone were interfaced with 
an ESP32 microcontroller. The ESP32 was programmed to 
detect the end of the audio signal and subsequently transmit 
a predefined binary sequence (e.g., 1010) via the laser to 
signal the end of transmission. On the receiver side, if the 
acknowledgment sequence is not received correctly or 
within the expected timeframe, a response is generated to 
indicate transmission failure or signal loss. This feedback 
mechanism enhances the reliability and integrity of the 
communication system by ensuring proper end-to-end data 
delivery. 
 
 
 
Fig. 5: Experimental Setup 
 
 
6.  Results 
 
The results demonstrate that text can be successfully 
transmitted using light signals via a laser module, with no 
observed error rate. The experimental setup consisted of 
two ESP32 modules acting as a transmitter and receiver, a 
laser diode for signal tran smission, and Solar panel for 
detection. In the air medium, the text was transmitted over 
a range of 5 meters, while in water, the range reached over 
1 meter.  
 
The experimental results highlight the importance of using 
filters and amplification circuits in laser -based audio 
transmission systems, as distortions and background noise 
were observed in the received audio output. The 
transmission was tested using a red laser over a distance of 
1 meter in a controlled environment. Under optimal 
conditions, no significant loss of the audio signal was 
detected; however, a noticeable level of noise persisted in 
the output. It was observed that the signal quality 
deteriorated with an increase in transmission distance, with 
higher noise levels and reduced clarity. These findings 
emphasize the need for effective filtering and noise 
reduction techniques to enhance the quality and range of 
underwater or free-space optical audio communication. 
 
Accurate text and audio reception was achieved without 
errors in the absence of obstacles, provided the laser and 
Solar panel were properly aligned. However, limitations

were observed in cases of misalignment or obstacles, 
leading to signal loss. These results validate the feasibility 
of using light signals for establishing a reliable 
communication system over significant distances in 
controlled environments. 
 
 
Fig. 6: Transmitting Text Signal 
 
 
 
Fig. 7: Receiving Text Signal 
 
 
7. Conclusion  
 
The results of the underwater communication system 
demonstrate successful real -time audio transmission 
using laser light. The transmitter efficiently modulates 
audio signals using pulse amplitude modulation 
(PAM), and the laser diode emits the signals thro ugh 
the water. The solar panel at the receiver side 
accurately detects the laser signals, which are then 
demodulated and amplified to produce clear audio 
output through the speaker. The system maintained 
communication over short distances in controlled 
water environments, with minimal signal degradation. 
However, challenges such as beam divergence, water 
turbidity, and alignment issues were observed, which 
could affect long-range communication.  
 
The study demonstrates that Li -Fi-based audio 
transmission is feasible but currently challenged by 
significant signal distortions and noise, necessitating 
the use of high-performance filtering and amplification 
techniques to ensure clear audio reception. 
Experimental observations suggest that employing 
higher-wavelength lasers, such as green or blue, can 
potentially extend the transmission range due to their 
better propagation characteristics in water. Accurate 
alignment between the laser source and the solar panel 
photodetector is also critical for minimizing data loss 
and maintaining reliable communication. 
Furthermore, this research highlights the limited 
availability of comprehensive studies on underwater 
Li-Fi communication, indicating a need for further 
exploration and development in this field. With 
continued innovation and optimization, Li -Fi has the 
potential to evolve into a robust and efficient 
communication system suitable for various underwater 
and line-of-sight applications. 
 
In conclusion, the proposed laser -based underwater 
communication system provides a cost -effective and 
reliable solution for short-distance audio transmission, 
making it suitable for applications like diver 
communication and underwater research, with 
potential for further optimization to enhance range and 
signal stability. 
 
 
8. Future Scope 
  The future scope of the underwater communication 
system includes several potential enhancements to 
improve its performance and applicability. Advanced 
laser technologies, such as green or blue lasers, can be 
implemented to minimize signal attenuation and 
extend the communication range in murky water. 
Incorporating adaptive beam alignment systems using 
servo motors or sensors can ensure consistent laser 
targeting, reducing signal loss due to misalignment. 
Additionally, integrating error corr ection algorithms 
and signal processing techniques can enhance data 
accuracy and resilience against underwater 
disturbances. Further developments can involve the 
use of machine learning models for noise reduction and 
real-time signal analysis. 
 
To enhance the functionality and reliability of the 
proposed Li -Fi communication system, future work 
can include the integration of an SD card module on 
the receiver side. This module would enable the 
storage of transmitted audio data, creating a permanent 
record of the communication. In the event of signal 
loss or transmission failure, the recorded data can be 
retransmitted automatically, eliminating the need for 
the user to repeat the message. Additionally, the 
incorporation of local storage facilitates the transfer of 
longer audio messages, extending the system’s 
applicability to scenarios requiring delayed playback, 
archival, or batch communication. This enhancement

would significantly improve the system's usability and 
robustness in real -world applications, particularly in 
environments where continuous or real -time 
communication may be disrupted. 
 
    The system can also be expanded for multi -node 
communication, supporting larger networks for 
underwater exploration and surveillance. Moreover, 
combining this laser -based system with acoustic 
communication can provide a hybrid solution for long-
range u nderwater data transmission. These 
advancements will significantly enhance the system’s 
reliability, making it suitable for applications in marine 
research, underwater robotics, and military operations.

external_metadata.title: 5 Mbps optical wireless communication with error correction coding for underwater sensor nodes
external_metadata.abstract: One issue with underwater sensors is how to efficiently transfer large amounts of data collected by the node to an interrogating platform such as an underwater vehicle. It is often impractical to make a physical connection between the node and the vehicle which suggests an acoustic or optical wireless solution. For large amounts of data, the high bandwidth of underwater optical wireless is an advantage. A small, low-cost platform to demonstrate the potential of an optical wireless communications interface for underwater sensor nodes is demonstrated. To enhance the reliability and robustness of the optical wireless communication digital signal processing and error correction techniques are used. The system was tested in 3 and 7.7 meter tanks at 5 Mbps with the turbidity of the water controlled by the addition of Maalox.

external_metadata.title: Real-Time Audio Transmission Using Visible Light Communication
external_metadata.abstract: RF technologies has facilitated communication including audio, images, video and data transmission. However, the RF spectrum is getting increasingly crowded, and alternative methods to transfer data need to be explored. In this paper, software-hardware co-design is implemented to design the audio data synchronization and transmission for an optical-through-air transceiver system. Besides audio transmission, the performance of the VLC system is verified through testing serial data transmission and text transmission. The experimental results show that the VLC system can achieve up to 4 Mb/s data rate using OOK modulation with red light. This system provides a practical step-by-step guidance for setting up a VLC system for data transmission.

external_metadata.abstract: This paper discusses a novel idea for transmission of voices in real time, underwater so that the system can be used by the deep sea divers for both lightning and data transfer applications simultaneously. Based on the comparison study, we make recommendations for the selection of the right colour of light for communication efficiency in specified underwater environments.

external_metadata.title: High-Speed Underwater Optical Wireless Communication with Advanced Signal Processing Methods Survey
external_metadata.abstract: Underwater wireless communication (UWC) technology has attracted widespread attention in the past few years. Compared with conventional acoustic underwater wireless communication technology, underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) technology has promising potential to provide high data rate wireless connections due to the large license-free bandwidth. Building a high-performance and reliable UOWC system has become the target of researchers and various advanced and innovative technologies have been proposed and investigated. Among them, better hardware such as transmitters and receivers, as well as more advanced modulation and signal processing techniques, are key factors in improving UOWC system performance. In this paper, we review the recent development in UOWC systems. In particular, we provide a brief introduction to different types of UOWC systems based on channel configuration, and we focus on various recent studies on advanced signal processing methods in UOWC systems, including both traditional non-machine learning (NML) equalizers and machine learning (ML) schemes based on neural networks. In addition, we also discuss the key challenges in UOWC systems for future applications.

tasks.source_abstract: One issue with underwater sensors is how to efficiently transfer large amounts of data collected by the node to an interrogating platform such as an underwater vehicle. It is often impractical to make a physical connection between the node and the vehicle which suggests an acoustic or optical wireless solution. For large amounts of data, the high bandwidth of underwater optical wireless is an advantage. A small, low-cost platform to demonstrate the potential of an optical wireless communications interface for underwater sensor nodes is demonstrated. To enhance the reliability and robustness of the optical wireless communication digital signal processing and error correction techniques are used. The system was tested in 3 and 7.7 meter tanks at 5 Mbps with the turbidity of the water controlled by the addition of Maalox.

tasks.source_abstract: RF technologies has facilitated communication including audio, images, video and data transmission. However, the RF spectrum is getting increasingly crowded, and alternative methods to transfer data need to be explored. In this paper, software-hardware co-design is implemented to design the audio data synchronization and transmission for an optical-through-air transceiver system. Besides audio transmission, the performance of the VLC system is verified through testing serial data transmission and text transmission. The experimental results show that the VLC system can achieve up to 4 Mb/s data rate using OOK modulation with red light. This system provides a practical step-by-step guidance for setting up a VLC system for data transmission.

tasks.source_abstract: This paper discusses a novel idea for transmission of voices in real time, underwater so that the system can be used by the deep sea divers for both lightning and data transfer applications simultaneously. Experiments were performed using white light, green and blue light respectively to transfer voice in real time in a water tank and the graphs were obtained. Based on the comparison study, we make recommendations for the selection of the right colour of light for communication efficiency in specified underwater environments.
